items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: No, he came to Milwaukee when I was with Charlie Elgar.

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…
. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. That's okay. You can cut that off. One. Two. You see, if you count and then pick back the notes up, it screws you up. Yeah. ¶ Thank you.

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: I went to Milwaukee with Charlie Elgar. He was from Chicago. He had a good band, too.

ctx.x: So he went downtown and bought one for me. And it was an old Conn clarinet, brand new, though. I took the thing home and (unintelligible) I started fooling around with it and I discovered that I could play more than I ever could on the clarinet. And I began to fool around with it and I began to like it again. And I woodshed -- you know, practicing -- we call it woodshedding, and I found out that it was coming around real good.

So he said, "You see, you little fool. You can play good. Why didn't you do that a long time ago?" I said, "Oh, I didn't like it like that. I didn't think I could do this kind of thing." So finally I started playing the clarinet and I put down the soprano altogether. The next thing you know I didn't want to play the tenor anymore. And so I kept on with the clarinet, and when I left Oliver and I came to New York -- and so I went to -- First I left Oliver and I went to Milwaukee with Charlie Elgar. He was from…
And I worked with Omer Simeon, and he's a fine clarinetist, too. Here's a boy that he really deserves a lot of praise but never did receive it, and he helped me a lot.

items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: Barnaby Godd, all of that. All of those boys are of that same school.

ctx.x: Homer Simeon studied from the young Thiel, too.

You find all of those boys are a product of those Thiel brothers. Albert Nicholas. And you find... Albert Nicholas. Barnaby Godd. Barnaby Godd, all of that. All of those boys are of that same school. If you compare their style, you find that they all follow pretty much in that same pattern of technique, which is different from the average planet player that you hear these days.
They're all dead now, that's why I'm asking you. I don't like to bother with a lot of questions.
